ev.q: Tianeptine exposure calls to U.S. poison control centers increased during 2014–2017
From 2014 through 2017, there was a statistically significant increase in calls related to exposure (p<0.001)
increased from five in 2014 to 38 in 2015, 83 in 2016, and 81 in 2017
Among the 93 tianeptine-only exposures with a known medical outcome, 50 (54%) had moderate outcomes.
the most commonly reported related clinical effects were neurologic (48.3%)
Persons reporting coexposure along with tianeptine were more likely to have major outcomes than those with tianeptine-only exposures.
CDC analyzed all exposure calls related to tianeptine reported by poison control centers to the National Poison Data System

methods_quotes.q: Frequencies for categorical variables and mean values for continuous variables were calculated using statistical software.
Tests for the trend for all tianeptine exposure calls and for calls related to intentional abuse or misuse during 2014–2017 were performed.
Fisher’s exact test was used to test for associations between reported outcome severity and tianeptine-only exposures versus tianeptine with coexposures, age group, and sex.
